title: Transcript coverage is reported, and zero coverage refuses (R1012)
body:
Implements `docs/plans/oracle/transcript-coverage-guard.md` — **OD-23 / R1012**, evidence **BL-27**. Replaces #158, which the review gate correctly blocked for having no blind-test authorship.

**The blind tests land first, and they found a defect.** A separate agent wrote them from the plan, OD-23 and BL-27 alone, in a worktree at a commit where `has_transcript` and `Coverage` do not exist — it could not read the implementation. Four of its tests then failed against mine.

It was right. The plan specifies `render_coverage` returns `"<n> of <m> <noun> had a cached transcript"`; I had baked two spaces of report indentation into that pure function. The two callers sit at different depths in their own reports, so a renderer carrying presentation cannot serve both. **The implementation was corrected, not the tests.**

That is the whole argument for the split, and it paid on the first slice.

**What R1012 does.** `Selection` gains `has_transcript`, set at the one line in `select_all` that can tell a cached empty transcript from the stand-in it substitutes — never inferred from the mention count, because a cached transcript naming no board is real coverage, not a miss. `Projection` carries a `Coverage` read off the selections rather than re-derived from disk, so the two stages print the same figure over populations that already differ.

Both stages print coverage on **every** run, zero included: a figure that appears only on failure is a figure nobody can compare across runs, which is exactly why BL-27's collapse was invisible. Zero coverage over a non-empty population refuses, names `fetch`, and exits 1 — and in `estimate` the refusal **replaces** the projection block rather than annotating it, because BL-27's finding is that a warning beside R7's stop sentence annotates it instead of separating it.

An empty population is not a refusal. Zero of zero is emptiness, not absence — the line R1005 already drew one layer down.

**Test-fixture edits** to `tests/test_select.py` and `tests/test_estimate.py` are mechanical consequences of the schema change. The schema test's key set gains `has_transcript` and stays an **exact-set** assertion; widening it to a subset check would retire the test that catches a stray key. My own R1012 tests are removed in favour of the blind ones rather than kept alongside them — keeping both would leave the suite half-tainted while reading as double coverage.

66 blind tests, 605 passing.
